subject: Introduction to Mechanical Engineering
title: Mechanics of Materials and Structures
sourceBasis: R-2025 ME25C03 Unit II scope: stress and strain; tensile, compressive and shear stresses; elasticity and plasticity; strength, toughness and hardness; bending, torsion, axial loading; simple structural analysis and design.
note: Original ACADRIX exam-practice problems based on the stated R-2025 scope and prescribed-book themes; not claimed official university questions or verified PYQs.

questions.question: Explain stress and strain in a loaded mechanical member and distinguish tensile, compressive and shear stress with suitable engineering examples.
solutionPlan: State normal and shear stress concepts.
Differentiate tensile, compressive and shear loading.
State relevant units and basic relations.

questions.question: A prismatic member is subjected to a concentric axial load. Determine the normal stress and deformation and discuss the assumptions used in the simple axial-loading model.
solutionPlan: Identify load, area, length and material properties.
Use sigma=P/A for uniform axial stress.
Use the appropriate elastic deformation relation when applicable.
State assumptions such as uniform section and axial loading.

questions.question: Analyze a simple compound member carrying an axial load and determine the load/stress sharing between its components under compatible deformation.
solutionPlan: Draw the member and identify components.
Write equilibrium of the applied load.
Relate stress and strain using material properties.

questions.question: Explain the elastic and plastic behaviour of an engineering material under loading, including what happens during loading and unloading beyond the elastic range.
solutionPlan: Explain permanent deformation after exceeding the elastic range.
Relate the concepts to component design and safety.

questions.question: Compare strength, toughness and hardness and explain why each property is important when selecting materials for mechanical components.
solutionPlan: Explain the type of resistance or behaviour represented.

questions.question: Explain the mechanics of bending in a beam subjected to transverse loading and describe how bending produces a distribution of normal stress across the section.
solutionPlan: Describe the neutral axis and stress distribution qualitatively.
Relate section geometry to bending resistance.

questions.question: Explain torsion of a mechanical member and determine the basic response of a circular shaft subjected to an applied torque.
solutionPlan: Identify the shaft geometry and material.
Use the appropriate elementary torsion relation when assumptions apply.

questions.question: Compare bending and torsion in mechanical members, including the type of loading, dominant stress, deformation mode and typical applications.
solutionPlan: Identify normal stress versus shear stress.

questions.question: Perform a basic structural analysis of a simply supported beam under a specified loading by determining support reactions and the resulting internal loading quantities.
solutionPlan: Determine internal shear force and bending moment as required.

questions.question: Analyze a simple pin-jointed truss under specified loads and determine member forces using an appropriate equilibrium-based method.
solutionPlan: Draw the complete truss and support reactions.
Choose method of joints or sections.
Classify members as tension or compression and check results.

questions.question: Explain the basic design procedure for selecting and proportioning a structural member so that it safely carries a specified load while satisfying strength and deformation requirements.
solutionPlan: Check strength against relevant stress limits.
Apply appropriate safety considerations and finalize the section.

questions.question: For a member subjected to different types of loading, identify the dominant stress state and explain how the loading mode influences material selection and component geometry.
solutionPlan: Determine whether normal or shear stress dominates.

questions.question: Discuss how strength, deformation, toughness and hardness influence the safe design of a mechanical component subjected to service loading.
solutionPlan: Relate strength to prevention of failure.
Relate hardness to wear and surface durability.

questions.question: Develop a simple engineering model for a load-carrying mechanical member and explain the complete sequence from loading definition through stress evaluation and design decision.
solutionPlan: Define the load case and constraints.
Compare with design requirements and state the decision.

questions.question: Solve an integrated mechanics-of-materials problem involving axial loading, bending or torsion, followed by an assessment of the member's suitability for the intended application.
solutionPlan: Apply the appropriate equilibrium and stress relations.
Conclude whether the design is acceptable and state possible improvements.

examChecklist: Start with a clear free-body diagram for structural problems.
Distinguish tensile, compressive and shear stress.
State assumptions before applying simplified stress relations.
For beams, connect transverse loading with shear and bending effects.
For shafts, connect torque with torsional shear stress and deformation.
For structural design, check both strength and acceptable deformation.
Interpret the final result in terms of safety and intended mechanical function.
